[[File:Great deltoidal hexecontahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a great deltoidal hexecontahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''great deltoidal hexecontahedron''' (or '''great sagittal ditriacontahedron''') is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[nonconvex great rhombicosidodecahedron]]. It is visually identical to the [[great rhombidodecacron]]. It has 60 intersecting [[cross quadrilateral]] faces, 120 edges, and 62 vertices. Its faces are darts. Part of each dart lies inside the solid, hence is invisible in solid models.

It is also called a ''great strombic hexecontahedron.''

== Proportions ==
The darts have two angles of <math>\arccos(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{5}\sqrt{5})\approx 18.699\,407\,085\,15^{\circ}</math>, one of <math>\arccos(-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{10}\sqrt{5})\approx 91.512\,394\,720\,74^{\circ}</math> and one of <math>360^{\circ}-\arccos(-\frac{1}{8}-\frac{9}{40}\sqrt{5})\approx 231.088\,791\,108\,96^{\circ}</math>. The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(\frac{-19+8\sqrt{5}}{41})\approx 91.553\,403\,672\,16^{\circ}</math>. The ratio between the lengths of the long and short edges is <math>\frac{21+3\sqrt{5}}{22}\approx 1.259\,463\,815\,11</math>.
